Definition: from G926; to weigh down (figuratively):--burden, charge, heavy, press.
BiblicalUsage: Bareo means to weigh down, to press with a burden. Paul says he was pressed out of measure in Asia so that he despaired even of life, and that we who are in this tabernacle groan, being burdened, while Jesus warns His disciples not to let their hearts be overcharged with surfeiting and cares, and finds His own disciples' eyes heavy with sleep in Gethsemane.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word tells the truth about pressure, because Paul was pressed beyond his strength and did not break. God let the weight fall so Paul would learn to trust the God who raises the dead, and I hold that the heaviest burdens are the ones that teach us we cannot carry ourselves.
